name: Background start restrictions
plain: Apps in the background cannot freely start foreground services or open screens.
meaning: Stops hidden activity from popping up or starting long tasks while the person is elsewhere. iOS goes further: apps can only launch for a few triggers, like location or push.

android.persistence: Exemptions: visible activity, high priority FCM message, exact alarm, active notification interaction, device owner
android.note: Android 12 blocks FGS starts from background except listed exemptions; Android 17 hardens IntentSender BAL

ios.persistence: iOS wakes apps only for specific events (push, location, BLE, geofence, background tasks)
ios.note: iOS has no equivalent start API; wake only on events

fields.name: android_exemptions
fields.range: FCM high, exact alarm, visible activity

limits.headline: Can't freely start work or open screens from the background
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when an app tries to start a service or screen while hidden
can: Start a foreground service from the background only in listed exemptions on Android 12 and newer
Open a screen from the background with a special display permission or a notification tap
Wake on events on iPhone, such as push or location
cannot: Start foreground services from the background at will on Android 12 and newer
Pop up screens over other apps with no exemption
Run on iPhone with an equivalent start call; it has none
limits.differs: Android 12 blocks background starts and Android 17 tightens it. iPhone has no start call, only event wake ups.

story.what_it_is: The phone stops apps in the background from suddenly starting visible services or opening screens.

marketing.name: Background start restrictions
marketing.pitch: Android limits when apps in the background can start foreground services, to stop surprise activity.

story.for_you: You notice it as fewer pop ups and less hidden work. An app you are not using cannot suddenly open a screen over your game or start a long task. That keeps the phone calm.
story.for_makers: Makers must start long work from a screen you are using or a clear event, like a tap or a push. Some tricks to start hidden work are blocked. Allowed exceptions are small and listed.

use_cases.example: A game cannot throw an ad screen over your video call from the background.
A chat app starts a call screen only through a high priority message you trigger.
A navigation app starts when you tap Start, not from the background.
A workout app starts tracking after a tap or an approved trigger.
A bad app tried to pop up fake login screens from the background, which the rules stop.
A driver app uses an allowed exemption while you are on a trip.

story.android_note: Android limits when background apps can start foreground services and open screens, with a list of exceptions.
story.ios_note: iPhone goes further and lets apps wake only for a few triggers, like location or push.

technical_bounds: Exemptions are narrow and change by version

history.change: Background execution limits, no background services
FGS start from background blocked except exemptions
Background activity launch hardened for IntentSender
